_doc: Which material each surface wears in Blender (and Unreal). Values are material keys from tools/blender/islandale3d/materials.
Resolution for a building mesh: buildings[first pattern matching the object's name].parts[part] -> defaults.parts[part];
a wall falls back to defaults.wall_kinds[the planner's wall kind] before defaults.parts.wall; a roof to defaults.roof_mats[roof material].
A part may be a key, or {"material": key, "params": {...}} for a tuned variant, or for walls
{"material": key, "wainscot": {"material": key, "height_m": 0.9}} for a stone base below a plain upper wall.
Patterns match the planner object's name case-insensitively as a substring. Site surfaces are keyed by role.

gathering prow._why: the sculptural cabin with the curved prow: carved kurinuki clay walls, charred-wood trim, charcoal standing-seam roof

family lantern._why: the octagon: fully clad in warm offset ledgestone (the user's first photo) under a verdigris copper pyramid roof

twin pod._why: the small butterfly-roof pod: rigidized bronze diamond sheet (the user's third screenshot), dark steel trim

elders._why: the calm, accessible wedge: warm white stucco over a cool stacked-stone wainscot, like the user's second photo

trees._why: the app's low-poly madrones: red peeling bark on the trunk and limbs, glossy evergreen leaves on the crown
